summary: Specifies the prospero URI scheme, originally defined in RFC 1738. It was written so RFC 1738 could be made obsolete while keeping information about the scheme on record. This document is historic.

eli5.summary: Prospero was an old system for finding files across computers. This memo keeps a record of its address style, like a museum label for a retired tool.

questions: what is the prospero uri scheme
subtitle: How to write addresses to access resources through the Prospero directory service.

tldr.problem: RFC 1738 was becoming obsolete but contained the definition of the Prospero URI scheme, which needed to remain on standards track.
tldr.mechanism: This document extracts and republishes the Prospero URI scheme specification, allowing RFC 1738 to be obsoleted while preserving the information about the scheme.
tldr.outcome: The Prospero protocol was never widely implemented and almost no Prospero servers are in use today, making this mostly a historical record of an early file-finding system.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Prospero URI scheme specifies how to write web addresses for resources accessed through the Prospero Directory Service. Originally defined in RFC 1738, this document preserves the specification so it remains available on standards track after RFC 1738 was made obsolete.

Prospero was a protocol for discovering and accessing networked resources, allowing clients to browse and retrieve files from distributed servers.
sections.eli5: Prospero was a way to find and get files from computers across the network. This memo saves the rules for writing Prospero addresses.

sections.title: Prospero URI Syntax
sections.content:
A Prospero URL takes the form prospero://<host>:<port>/<hsoname>;<field>=<value>. If the port is omitted, it defaults to 1525. No username or password is allowed in the URL.

The <hsoname> is the host-specific object name in the Prospero protocol, suitably encoded. This name is opaque and interpreted only by the Prospero server. The semicolon ";" is reserved and may not appear without quoting in the <hsoname>.

After the <hsoname>, optional fields and values associated with a Prospero link may be specified. Each field/value pair is separated by a ";" (semicolon), with the name and value separated by a "=" (equal sign). For example, the OBJECT-VERSION field can identify a specific version of an object. A slash "/" may appear in the <hsoname> without quoting; slashes do not necessarily indicate hierarchical structure on the server.
sections.eli5: Prospero addresses point to a server and a named resource, optionally with version or other details. Unlike some web addresses, the structure inside the name is not guaranteed to mean anything.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Prospero uses passwords in the clear for authentication and offers no privacy. The Prospero protocol itself is considered unsafe by current standards.

Standard URI security considerations discussed in RFC 3986 also apply to Prospero URIs.
sections.eli5: Prospero sends passwords unencrypted and does not hide messages, so it was not secure even when it was in use.
